ARCH 121.name: Visual Communications I
ARCH 121.description: Development of two- and three-dimensional graphic communications skills. Bulletin lists this as a companion course to ARCH 131 (Basic Design Studio I) -- modeled as one-directional (ARCH 131 requires ARCH 121 concurrently, not vice versa) since the engine's same-term scheduling can't resolve a mutual two-way concurrent requirement; both are scheduled in Semester 1 regardless.

ARCH 122.name: Visual Communications II
ARCH 122.description: Digital graphic communications tools for architectural practice. Bulletin lists this as a companion course to ARCH 132 (Basic Design Studio II) -- modeled as one-directional (ARCH 132 requires ARCH 122 concurrently, not vice versa), same reasoning as ARCH 121/131.

ARCH 131.name: Basic Design Studio I
ARCH 131.description: Introduction to architectural design concepts in a studio environment.

ARCH 132.name: Basic Design Studio II
ARCH 132.description: Continuation of Basic Design Studio, emphasizing craftsmanship and construction methods.

ARCH 203.name: Materials and Building Construction I
ARCH 203.description: Introduction to common architectural building materials and associated methods.

ARCH 210.name: Ideas Across Time in Architecture and Urbanism
ARCH 210.description: Transversal history of architectural and urban ideas across time. Bulletin recommends a prior survey course in architectural history (not enforced).

ARCH 231.name: Architectural Design I
ARCH 231.description: Design of limited environments within defined constraints. Bulletin also lists this as a companion course to ARCH 203 -- modeled one-directional (ARCH 203 requires ARCH 231 concurrently, not vice versa) since the engine can't resolve a mutual two-way concurrent requirement; both are scheduled in the same semester regardless.

ARCH 232.name: Architectural Design II
ARCH 232.description: Continuation of second-year architectural design curriculum. Bulletin also lists this as a companion course to ARCH 204 -- modeled one-directional (ARCH 204 requires ARCH 232 concurrently, not vice versa), same reasoning as ARCH 231/203.

ARCH 311W.name: Architectural and Planning Theories
ARCH 311W.description: Writing-intensive seminar exploring critical-thinking skills in architectural theory.

ARCH 312.name: Non-Western Architectural Traditions Elective
ARCH 312.description: Non-Western architectural traditions elective (placeholder entry; exact topic varies by offering).

ARCH 317.name: Theory of Modern Japanese Architecture
ARCH 317.description: Development of modern Japanese architecture from the Meiji Restoration to the present.

ARCH 331.name: Architectural Design III
ARCH 331.description: Development of the design process through organizational methodologies. Bulletin lists an enforced concurrent 'AE 211', which could not be confirmed to exist in the current catalog -- not modeled.

ARCH 332.name: Architectural Design IV
ARCH 332.description: Continuation of third-year design curriculum, emphasizing the building thoroughly considered.

ARCH 380.name: Building Environmental Systems I
ARCH 380.description: Building thermal environment and heating/cooling systems.

ARCH 381.name: Building Environmental Systems II
ARCH 381.description: Illumination, acoustics, fire protection, electrical and plumbing design.

ARCH 480.name: Technical Systems Integration
ARCH 480.description: Synthesis of structural, mechanical, and electrical systems integration. Bulletin describes this as typically taken alongside ARCH 332/ARCH 381 -- not modeled as a hard concurrent requirement since ARCH 332 -> ARCH 381 -> ARCH 480 already forms a same-term dependency chain and adding a fourth edge back to ARCH 332 would create an unresolvable circular concurrency in the engine.

ARCH 491.name: Architectural Design Research Studio - Directed
ARCH 491.description: In-depth architectural inquiry with propositional thesis development. Catalog range is 12-18cr (repeatable, max 18); modeled here at 6cr for its first enrollment.

ARCH 492H.name: Architectural Design Studio
ARCH 492H.description: Continuation of the design studio sequence with concentration and specialization options (Honors).

ARCH 451.name: Architectural Professional Practice
ARCH 451.description: Study of architectural practice in today's society.

ARCH 499A.name: Rome Study-Architectural Design
ARCH 499A.description: Design studio addressing new construction within historic contexts in Rome. Bulletin lists ARCH 499A/B/C as a mutually-required package taken together during the required Rome semester -- not modeled as pairwise concurrent requirements since all three referencing each other would create an unresolvable circular concurrency in the engine; the shared prereq gate (ARCH 332 + ARCH 480) already ensures none is reachable early.

ARCH 499B.name: Architectural Analysis
ARCH 499B.description: Analytical decomposition of architecture as amplified and embodied in cities. Part of the ARCH 499A/B/C Rome package -- see ARCH 499A's note on why pairwise concurrency isn't modeled.

ARCH 499C.name: Urban Studies
ARCH 499C.description: History of Rome presented through cartographic and morphological analysis. Part of the ARCH 499A/B/C Rome package -- see ARCH 499A's note on why pairwise concurrency isn't modeled.
